newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Luxembourg PM sees success at Amsterdam EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg PM sees success at Amsterdam EU summit.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker, who brokered an initial deal between France and Germany on budgetary rigour in December, said on Sunday he believed there would be success at the EU summit in Amsterdam.

Arriving for the summit to be held on Monday and Tuesday, Juncker was asked whether he had been negotiating with Paris and Bonn over the new dispute which blew up when France demanded more emphasis be placed on employment.
"I had sufficient contact in order to know that we will have success," Juncker, who is also finance minister, said.

Juncker was among the first EU leaders arriving for the June 16-17 summit, which has been overshadowed by a Franco-German rift over the new French government's insistence on putting more emphasis on jobs in the drive towards economic and monetary union (EMU).
EU finance ministers were to meet on the issue later on Sunday.
The disagreement between Bonn and Paris, which normally form a strong alliance at the centre of EU integration, was prompted by this month's socialist victory in French parliamentary elections.
The split threatens to dominate the two-day meeting which was supposed to culminate in agreement on a new treaty setting Europe's course for the next century.
But new French premier Lionel Jospin has told his partners he wants greater emphasis given to creating jobs in the 15-member bloc. He is hostile to the economic austerity required to qualify for EMU.

An EU diplomat said the big problem for the leaders at the summit was to find a way of dealing with France's demands to resurrect funding for Trans-European Networks (TENs) as a way for creating jobs.
"Nobody wants to commit themselves to spending at this summit," he said. "To know exactly how to deal with (TENs) is the problem.
TENs are infrastructure projects, mainly communications links, that have been approved by the EU but lie relatively unfunded.
